items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: And Harry Gray, the president of our union, was up there. He was playing with us then.

ctx.x: It's strange that Wycliffe wasn't recorded.

I don't know why. Because we had a very good band. He always insisted. One good thing about him. He always insisted in getting good man. And he made the owners. They'd come up with, when they wanted to come up with that three or four or five pieces. He'd tell them, no, my band is eight, ten, whatever it was. And that's the way it sounds. And that's what's going to do your business. And he was a good talker in getting jobs. Because we went up to Blue Mountain. The Blue Chipper on the Blue Mountain Road, Milwaukee.…
Now, Jabba wasn't with you, was he?
